title: Naturality of objectwise normalized fibre pullback
statement: Let k,l,R be as in [lem-per-normalized-pullback-objects]. Fix normalized fibres ω and any objectwise comparison package p satisfying the unit and integral local normalization of that node. For every finite coefficient field A/Q_l, g:Y→X, geometric point y:Spec κ→Y and heart arrow f:F→G, the square of p.component at F and G commutes: ω_y(g*f) followed by p_G equals p_F followed by ω_(y g)(f). This asserts only naturality of the existing objectwise family, not existence or identity/composition coherence.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4),(6); Remark 6.8.15; finite pullback stalk normalization, Stacks Tag 03Q1, etale-cohomology.tex lemma-stalk-pullback(3)

proof.text: Choose a common adapted stratification and a pointed affine etale refinement for F and G. Full faithfulness of raw lisse lattice rationalization on this qcqs refinement represents the restricted f by an integral lattice arrow divided by a uniformizer power.

Naturality of the finite-level inverse-image stalk isomorphism commutes with the integral arrow. Applying inverse-limit projections gives the integral limit-map equality. The fractions equation of ω multiplies both sides by the same inverse uniformizer power. Equal fractional representatives have cleared difference killed by a uniformizer power, which becomes invertible after rationalization.

The local-normalization equations of p identify the two sides with these conjugated rational limit maps. The common intrinsic fibre identifications compare every refinement, lattice and chart, and cancel from both sides. Thus the equality holds on the original F and G, without assuming torsion-free integral Hom.

lean.statement:
theorem objectwise_normalized_pullback_naturality
    (ω : Fibres (k := k) l R) (p : ObjectwiseNormalizedPullback l R ω)
    (A : Type u) [Field A] [Algebra ℚ_[l] A] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] A]
    {X Y : FiniteTypeBase k} (g : Y.scheme ⟶ X.scheme)
    (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [IsAlgClosed κ] (y : Spec (.of κ) ⟶ Y.scheme)
    {F G : NormalizedFibre.Heart l A (base l X)} (f : F ⟶ G) :
    ((ω A Y).point κ y).functor.map ((heartPull l A R g).map f) ≫
        (p.component A g κ y G).hom =
      (p.component A g κ y F).hom ≫ ((ω A X).point κ (y ≫ g)).functor.map f
